# History: RHM (Random Hierarchy Model)

*Auto-generated big-picture pass. Traces the shape of the work, not the day-to-day. See [README.md](README.md) for the living technical summary and [FILES.md](FILES.md) for the full file index.*

## Why this substrate exists

RHM was adopted after natural-language experiments hit a wall: vocab reduction turned out to be a channel intervention (moves β, not γ), and spectral denoising confounded the statistics it was meant to measure. RHM trades realism for **control** — a generative process with known ground-truth hierarchy, exact ancestry traces, and a tunable DGP (depth `L`, synonymy `m`, branching `s`, vocab `v`). Almost every subsequent arc exists because some ambiguity in language or MuJoCo work needed a substrate where the confound could be cut cleanly. That trade is still being cashed in three months later.

## Era 1 — instruments for reading a forward model (through 2026-06-23)

The opening arc measured how a forward model's (FM) residual `a_j = FM(a_i) + r` reflects the main model's computation: scaling-exponent sweeps (m dominates depth 3:1), residual rank, the L→m regime transition, per-level loss decomposition, and a family of loss-reweighting objectives (label smoothing, focal loss, FM-surprise weighting). The throughline belief formed here — **the FM residual is a real, structured readout of what the model has and hasn't learned, not architectural noise** — becomes load-bearing for everything downstream. Full numeric detail is in [README.md](README.md)'s own Results section; it isn't re-litigated here.

**Residual rank was later found to be reading the wrong thing.** [`residual_decomposition/README.md`](residual_decomposition/README.md) (2026-07-27) showed the old entropy-rank instrument conflates *shape* and *magnitude* — it can rise 17× while relative residual shrinks 17×, and the `R_act ≈ R_comp + R_res` arithmetic it was built on doesn't hold. The replacement is two decoupled numbers: **β** (a capacity-invariant exponent of `res_var ∝ act_var^β`) and **`R_res_participation`** (frontier dimensionality in the model's own basis). This *reframed*, rather than reversed, three standing negatives (the original rank sweep, "full-rank yet cosine 0.97" language residuals, and an MJC contact-residual result) — all three were reading a saturated FM's noise floor. β/`R_res_participation` become the standard instrument for every later arc that needs to read "how much is really being learned."

## Era 2 — the ratchet: compounding self-distillation fails, and why (through 2026-06-29)

[`ratchet/README.md`](ratchet/README.md) asked whether the MNIST gated wake-sleep ratchet (34%→48% over 4 cycles) also compounds on RHM. It reproduced every *qualitative* MNIST dynamic — gate closing, FM tracking, robustness dissociation — but never the *magnitude* (peaks ~1%, no compounding). The arc eliminated capacity, task structure, the distillation bottleneck, and FM-cosine regime one at a time; a FOMAML diagnostic closed it: **on stationary data, no outer objective makes FM-predictability pressure improve compositional NTP.** The belief that survives is narrower and more useful than the one that died — compounding needs a *moving frontier*, which stationary RHM cannot supply by itself. This single conclusion is the hinge for the entire back half of the RHM program: the active/sculpting, latent-loop, specialization, and minting lines all exist to manufacture or search for that missing frontier motion.

FM-as-regularizer (2026-07-01) and the complexodynamics reading of saved trajectories (2026-07-07) sit in this era too, both confirming the residual is a real, DGP-aligned quantity that pressure can sculpt (see [README.md](README.md) for detail) — reinforcing Era 1's belief rather than complicating it.

## Era 3 — can the frontier be moved by allocation alone? No.

[`specialization/README.md`](specialization/README.md) (2026-07-16) tested the ratchet's implied next question directly: can concentrating training — by breadth (subtree restriction) or by loss weighting (deep-token reweighting) — push the depth frontier deeper *somewhere*? Both are inert-to-harmful; only a *direct* deep label recruits depth, and even that fails to specialize (Student-B-broad beats Student-A-narrow) because **RHM's single shared ruleset has no domain-specific deep structure to concentrate on.** This is the first sharp RHM-vs-language disanalogy in the program, and a 2026-07-18 reframe turns it from a deficiency into the question that motivates a genuinely heterogeneous DGP — the direct ancestor of `directed_sculpting`'s distractor channels and `minting`'s support-oracle question.

The [confabulation test](confabulation/README.md) (2026-07-22) runs in parallel, applying the Era-1 residual/FM machinery to introspection: is a self-report reading the residual (genuine access) or reconstructing it from the FM's range (a learned self-theory)? IMPL is the only target with a first-person advantage over a capacity-matched observer; closing the wake-sleep loop changes *how well* the model knows itself, not *what* there is to know. [`confabulation/temporal/`](confabulation/temporal/README.md) later sharpens this: the belief-revision "charge" the residual carries is real but **public** — a third-party observer reads it exactly as well as self-report does.

## Era 4 — directed sculpting: porting an active loop, and a recurring lesson about instruments

[`directed_sculpting/README.md`](directed_sculpting/README.md) (2026-07-28 onward) ports the `value = lprog × visits` outer loop from a MuJoCo experiment (E3) onto RHM. The naive port is a **confounded null by construction**: RHM rule usage is uniform, so `visits` is flat and the loop collapses to `lprog` alone — the exact numeric form of Era 3's disanalogy. Distractor channels, support-fixed drift, and a repair-cost instrument fix this, but building the repair-cost instrument itself surfaces the arc's most repeated lesson: **raw cross-entropy is provably blind to support-fixed drift**, and the repaired-vs-reference gap was independently inflated 2× by ordinary continued training. Every subsequent cut in this arc repeats the same shape of event — a plausible positive turns out to be an artifact of the measuring instrument, gets caught (usually by a pre-registered gate or falsifier), and gets repaired:

- [`full_loop/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/README.md): the reward-free relevance value is a genuine smoking gun (13–18× separation of real tokens from distractors, 76% of oracle recovery). But a first read of the "reducibility" tap was **exactly inverted** by fixed-budget noise; grading arms in their own drifted world inflated an apparent expansion effect by ~65%; and both drift-dependent climbing/expansion predictions came back negative until starving samples-per-event (fixed drift magnitude) produced the arc's first true climbing positive.
- [`metering_sweep/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/metering_sweep/README.md): the idea doc's central prediction — curation value shrinks as data gets abundant — had never actually been tested (the "meter" was a no-op). Made real, round 1's falsifier fired **with the wrong sign** (prize rose with budget); round 2 found this was itself a compute confound, and iso-compute the prize is humped, falling at the abundant end — the original prediction, correctly measured.
- [`endo_expansion/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/endo_expansion/README.md) and [`endogenous_expansion/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/endogenous_expansion/README.md): two parallel cuts, run without contact, converge on the same answer — an endogenous evaluative grader **does** expand the belief (19–34% of an external teacher's lift) — and independently discover the same landmine: belief participation-ratio, the arc's headline "expansion" metric, rises just as much for a zero-information random target as for a good one. PR detects whether a pathway exists, not whether what flows through it is any good; it is retired as a ranker across the whole prior arc.
- [`minting/README.md`](minting/README.md): can a learner escape the ceiling by minting and self-filtering its own data? Filtering by the true rule table prevents damage (verified arm ties no-minting) but real data at equal volume still wins by 17×. The mechanism: a rule-table filter is a **support oracle** ("is this possible"), not a **density oracle** ("how often should this occur") — and NTP is density matching, so a support filter can delete harmful mass but cannot manufacture the missing distributional information.
- [`partial_hetero/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/partial_hetero/README.md) and [`shared_surface/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/partial_hetero/shared_surface/README.md): fills the gap between one shared ruleset (inert) and fully independent channels (costly). The predicted monotone transfer-vs-sharing curve never moves — even at generatively identical channels — and the diagnosis is a missing shared vocabulary at the level the splice cuts. A bottom-up splice recovers the shared code but the transfer curve still sits inside the instrument's own noise floor: geometry fixed, readout is now the bottleneck.
- [`level_moves/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/level_moves/README.md) / [`level_ladder/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/level_moves/level_ladder/README.md): an apparent value-function preference for higher hierarchy levels **corrected itself** — a depth-matched null channel showed the same rise, meaning it was span, not abstraction. A matched-span twin control isolates a real, smaller abstraction preference, graded by whether a move at that level can actually reach the error.
- [`composed_loop/README.md`](directed_sculpting/full_loop/composed_loop/README.md): combining the endogenous judge with the level-indexed action space is a large **negative** interaction (a scalar terminal-success signal carries no depth information). The one clean positive: self-directed *exploration* (what the value's own rollouts see), not self-directed *judgment*, recovers 45% of a privileged teacher's value with zero labels.

**Standing belief exiting Era 4**: self-direction (endogenous grading, self-minted data, self-chosen abstraction level) is not free — it reliably prevents damage or redistributes existing capability, and only occasionally, under specific conditions (a grounded evaluative grader; exploration rather than judgment), produces genuine expansion. Read literally, that's a partial reversal of Era 2's pessimism — but the mechanism each time is narrower than "self-improvement," which is why each result required a purpose-built instrument to see.

## Era 5 — belief revision vs. surprisal: a signal that keeps sharpening but never cashes in

A second chain asks whether a model's internal "I was wrong" signal is separable from raw token surprisal, and whether it can be harvested to teach.

- [`endogenous_teacher/README.md`](endogenous_teacher/README.md): Gate 0 finds the FM residual and token surprisal are ~independent and *anti*-localized (residual peaks where text is nearly free, not where it's surprising). The obvious next step — weight NTP loss by the residual — is a clean, pre-registered null. The [`cancellation/`](endogenous_teacher/cancellation/README.md) child tries routing the signal through the forward path instead; the corollary-discharge mechanism replicates a prior ViT result closely, but the downstream payoff doesn't scale with it — the diagnosis is that a same-timestep depth FM's residual can only ever mean "I lacked capacity," never "I was wrong."
- [`conditional_revision/README.md`](conditional_revision/README.md): fixes exactly that — shifts the FM's target to a genuine one-token-ahead prediction, and builds an *exact* belief-propagation oracle against RHM's known parse structure (discovering along the way that RHM's latent graph is a **hypertree**, not a pairwise tree, so a naive pairwise KL is simply wrong). **Gate B**, the pre-registered primary kill, finds the model's revision readout does separate reducible from irreducible surprise, but only at d2–d3, never above — the binding constraint is **belief depth**, not the conditioning-gap fix. Children ([`sculpt_slip/`](conditional_revision/sculpt_slip/README.md), [`rule_family/`](conditional_revision/rule_family/README.md), [`aleatoric_fraction/`](conditional_revision/aleatoric_fraction/README.md), [`local_loss/`](conditional_revision/local_loss/README.md), [`synonym_retention/`](conditional_revision/synonym_retention/README.md)) each try to cash the signal in — for gating, in-context reducibility, or an auxiliary loss — and each is killed for a distinct, specific reason (an FM that's bias- not variance-dominated; a training signal that's ~90% gauge-collapse; a base model that already sheds the needed distinction).
- [`question_model/README.md`](question_model/README.md): adds a third exactly-computable term — "question-news," what a demand distribution drifting by an OU process is currently asking. NTP builds an implicit tracker only above an evidence-density threshold; an explicit tracker's one real payoff is warm-starting a fast component at context entry, not the slow-component role it was designed for; a demand-keyed self-knowledge readout is a vacuous null because the competence heterogeneity it presupposes never existed for this unmetered model.

**Standing belief**: belief-revision is real, separable from surprisal, and exactly measurable where the model holds a belief at all — but every attempt across this whole chain to cash it in for direct learning gain (weighting, injection, gating) has come back null. The signal keeps getting more precisely characterized; it has not yet become useful.

## Era 6 — practice: the one arc where self-direction clearly pays off

[`practice/README.md`](practice/README.md) (2026-08-14 onward) ports an "étude" compile-op (δ-silence certificate, selection over averaging, scoring under the consumption distribution) from a MuJoCo motor-learning line onto RHM sculpting — and this is the arc that most directly contradicts Era 4/5's caution. State-conditioned commitment beats state-independent commitment 1.8–3.0×; earning a mined action vocabulary ([`practice/ratchet/`](practice/ratchet/README.md) — distinct from Era 2's `ratchet/`) recovers 68–98% of what being handed the DGP's own vocabulary buys. [`practice/ear/`](practice/ear/README.md) and [`practice/recital/`](practice/recital/README.md) find no *internal* pacing signal can price time-at-the-bottom-of-the-ladder correctly, but a fixed bottom-heavy schedule is rank 1 regardless — self-direction over *what* to commit works; self-direction over *when* does not. [`practice/tall/`](practice/tall/README.md) hits a hard structural ceiling (endogenous pacers cannot outrun the earnable range). Round 6, the crossed [`transpose`](practice/transpose/FILES.md) × [`setlist`](practice/setlist/FILES.md) pair (written up in [`typed_gaps/README.md`](practice/typed_gaps/README.md)), finds a double dissociation: drifting *what's true* only the dense learner degrades; drifting *what's asked* only the evaluative re-selection channel fires. The conclusion is that **the conditioning gap is typed** — one organ per currency of change, not one generic "surprise" signal (a direct echo of Era 5's failure to find a single scalar that works everywhere).

The two newest rounds extend this to the *addressing layer* over commitments, not just the commitments themselves. [`practice/fourwall/README.md`](practice/fourwall/README.md) decomposes "whittle toward the pure form" into three distinct, separately-priced operations — merge, re-key, retire — and shows a free, spurious surface index (a token that's a perfect correlate of truth until it isn't) produces *rational* stickiness, not a bug, once the migration gate is graded on consumption rather than coverage. [`practice/reread/`](practice/reread/README.md) (plus its [`lm/`](practice/reread/lm/README.md) twin) and [`practice/merge/`](practice/merge/README.md) show "free data" — a re-readable archive, self-generated practice — bifurcates into a competence currency that fully renews and a new-vocabulary-mining currency that decays to ~0 without re-arming, with renewability capped by a hard corpus-size wall rather than a soft tax.

**Net read across Era 6**: unlike minting or the endogenous grader, structured self-practice under a *priced, certificate-gated* commitment mechanism reliably captures most of an oracle's value. The difference from Era 4/5's negatives appears to be exactly that pricing/gating structure — compiling under a consumption-scored certificate, rather than self-training or self-weighting blindly.

## The throughline

Read across all six eras, the RHM program is one long, repeatedly re-asked question — **can a learner improve using only signals it generates or judges itself, without an external oracle?** — tested from every angle (self-distillation, self-allocation, self-minted data, self-judged reward, self-detected surprise, self-paced practice). The answer is almost never a flat no: self-direction reliably *prevents damage* and *redistributes* existing capability, and *occasionally* produces genuine expansion, but only when the self-generated signal is pinned to something exact and cheaply verifiable (a support oracle, a certificate, an exact BP identity) rather than free-floating (a scalar reward, a learned self-theory, raw self-training). The other consistent thread, almost methodological rather than substantive, is that **nearly every positive result in this history first appeared as an instrument artifact** — inverted taps, sign-flipped falsifiers, compute-confounded sweeps, a rank metric blind to magnitude — and survived only after a pre-registered gate or a matched control caught and repaired it. The practice arc's certificate-gating and the sculpting arc's repeated instrument repairs are the same discipline applied to two different objects: verify before you believe the machine is measuring what you think it's measuring.
